thread:
mike_sales: FYI inbound from OmniCart. They finished SSO onboarding but their app gets 403 calling our API. Console shows an API key was created. Can someone triage? org_id=org_omnicart_842 @ana_k
provisioning-bot: Provisioner log snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T10:12:03Z] create_key request: org=org_omnicart_842 requested_project=omnicart-prod
[2026-03-15T10:12:04Z] fallback: org mapping missing -> default_project=internal-tools
[2026-03-15T10:12:04Z] created_key id=sk_live_abc123 assigned_project=internal-tools status=active
```
ana_k: On it — thanks @mike_sales. Quick question: did they sign up via Okta SSO or a manual invite?
mike_sales: Okta SSO, SCIM on. They passed us an assertion. I can share the OIDC assertion if needed.
lee_infra: I can see the same log. There's a provisioning path that falls back to `internal-tools` when org->project mapping lookup fails. We had a partial rollout of a mapping-fix last week; looks like prod didn't pick it up in one region.
sara_devops: If we want to unblock fast, I can manually rebind the key to the correct project. Command I will run:```
provisioner rebind --key sk_live_abc123 --to-project omnicart-prod --actor lee_infra
# expected output:
# OK: key sk_live_abc123 bound to project omnicart-prod
```
mike_sales: Go for it, please. I've told the customer we're investigating.
provisioning-bot: Running rebind...
```
[2026-03-15T10:15:01Z] rebind_request key=sk_live_abc123 -> omnicart-prod by=lee_infra
[2026-03-15T10:15:02Z] audit: previous_project=internal-tools new_project=omnicart-prod
[2026-03-15T10:15:02Z] result=success
```
ana_k: After rebind, can the customer still see 403? There are two failure modes: project mismatch (403) or scope mismatch (401/insufficient_scope). Logs from their app?
mike_sales: Customer sent one snippet (redacted):```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
content-type: application/json
{"error":"project_permission_denied","message":"Key not valid for org omnicart-prod"}
```
ana_k: That matches project mismatch. Rebind should resolve. @mike_sales ask the customer to restart the process and clear cached creds. Also ensure they replace the key if they have it embedded in envs.
lee_infra: Note — rebind changed project but key scopes stayed as `read:models`. If they need write access we should issue a new key with requested scopes. Also I'll open a follow-up to disable fallback assignment entirely and add an alert when fallback occurs.
sara_devops: Created a replacement key anyway to be safe:```
[2026-03-15T10:17:40Z] create_key id=sk_live_new_9f2 project=omnicart-prod scopes=[read:models,write:inference] created_by=sara_devops
```
mike_sales: Customer confirmed new key works, their integration returns 200 and tokens start responding. :tada: They said the retry logic in their app picked up the key automatically after we posted it.
ana_k: Great. Action items: (1) revoke sk_live_abc123 or keep for audit? (2) add monitoring alert on fallback creation; (3) patch provisioning service in remaining region.
lee_infra: I'll revoke the old key once we've verified no clients rely on it. Creating an infra ticket for the rollback gap and the mapping fix PR: https://redwood.internal/p/infra/provisioner-mapping-fix (assigning to @lee_infra).
mike_sales: I'll follow up with the customer on rotation and confirm closure.
ana_k: Thanks everyone. I'll add a short postmortem in #support later with repro steps. For the record: root cause = provisioning fallback assignment when org->project mapping lookup returned null, causing keys to land in `internal-tools`.
provisioning-bot: Note: fallback event recorded id=fbe0a6a alert=none -> raising ticket flow as requested.
sara_devops: PR to require explicit mapping or fail fast: DRAFT open at https://redwood.internal/p/infra/provisioner-failfast. Tagging for review.
mike_sales: Customer happy, closing loop. :white_check_mark:
